_comment: Biscuit appended-block READ-PATH golden (doc 19 §4/§6, D98). The session-token library reads the EFFECTIVE (deepest) claim set off an attenuated Biscuit through biscuit-go's debug Code() renderer (sessiontoken_biscuit.go: claimsTermRe over b.Code()[n-1]), because biscuit-go v2.2.0 surfaces appended blocks only through that render path, not the authority Query path. That makes the renderer's BLOCK SHAPE a load-bearing parse contract: a biscuit-go upgrade that changes how an appended block renders (spacing, the session_token_claims(N, "...") term form, quoting, the Block { } scaffold) would silently break the read path. This fixture PINS that shape so such a drift fails LOUDLY at test time instead of mis-parsing a token in production. The biscuit-go version stays pinned at v2.2.0 (go.mod); this golden is the tripwire if it ever moves. Synthetic only (D50): synthetic UUIDs/role/task, a fresh in-test Ed25519 key, no secrets anywhere — the rendered payload is base64url(JSON of a synthetic claim record).

appended_block._comment: The EXACT biscuit-go v2.2.0 Code() render of one appended attenuation block carrying a session_token_claims(depth, payload) fact, with the base64url payload substituted by %PAYLOAD%. Tabs and newlines are literal; %PAYLOAD% is the only variable. The read path's claimsTermRe must match against this shape; a renderer that emits a different scaffold breaks the assertion.

round_trip._comment: A full mint->attenuate->Verify round trip pinned on a SYNTHETIC claim set. The base64url payload is a deterministic function of the child claim JSON, so it is pinned exactly; the read path must decode it back to these claims through the Code() render. This catches both a renderer-shape drift (the appended_block template above) AND a payload-encoding drift (the base64url/JSON claim encoding) in one self-checking case.
